Next month the 26th marks the one-year anniversary of the Tai Po Wang Fuk Court fire. The independent committee investigating the fire is expected to submit its report to the Chief Executive before the end of October. Recent reports have indicated that the government has already initiated the Heads of Department Accountability System to investigate the administrative responsibility for the major fire, and has redeployed Administrative Officers to assist. Chief Executive John Lee did not respond today (the 6th) on whether the system has been activated, stating that the government has made a series of arrangements and will implement reforms and pursue accountability as soon as possible after the report is submitted. The Stanley luxury residence One Stanley has been exposed for steel reinforcement not matching the plans. Lee said the Buildings Department is investigating the case and he has asked the Development Bureau to monitor the investigation. With multiple projects being exposed for problems one after another, he said he attaches great importance to the construction quality of building projects in Hong Kong, which concerns the professional standards, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will strictly enforce the law.

It is nearly a year since the Wang Fuk Court fire, and the independent committee is expected to submit its report before the end of October. (File photo)

Earlier media reports said that two Administrative Officers—former Under Secretary for Security Mok Kwan-yu, and Commissioner for Sports Choi Kin-heen-lim, would provide support work to an investigation小组 under the Public Service Commission, dedicated to preparatory work for administrative accountability.

Before attending the Executive Council meeting today, Chief Executive John Lee met the press and was asked whether the reports were true? With the Heads of Department Accountability System investigation underway, does it mean that even if there is a report, accountability involving officials will not come to a conclusion immediately, and how long must the public wait?

Lee said he had made it clear from the start that after the independent committee submits its report, he would actively study and follow up on the recommendations, carry out reforms and announce specifics. He did not directly confirm whether a Political Affairs Officer has already been redeployed to prepare the preliminary investigation work, only saying that "the government has been making a series of arrangements during this period", emphasising that after the report is submitted, "within a short period, we will as soon as possible implement comprehensive reforms and pursue accountability" in accordance with the content, and will make detailed announcements at that time.

Lee said that after the independent committee submits its report, reforms and accountability will be implemented as soon as possible. (File photo)

Lee reiterated once again that improvement measures are urgent, so when the Policy Address was delivered in September, he announced 7 priority improvement measures, including banning smoking on construction sites, strengthening regulation of fire service installations, strengthening disciplinary action and punishment for professionals and contractors, improving compliance operation of owners' corporations, studying the criminalisation of bid-rigging, providing tendering and evaluation services for the first time, formulating pre-qualification lists for consultants and contractors, and studying plans to better assist the public with the professional nature of projects.

According to records, the Public Service Commission is an independent statutory advisory body that advises the Chief Executive on matters relating to the appointment, promotion and discipline of civil servants. The Heads of Department Accountability System was proposed by Chief Executive John Lee in last year's Policy Address, establishing a two-tier investigation mechanism according to the seriousness of departmental problems. If the problem is less serious in nature, such as an isolated incident, the first-tier investigation will be conducted by the head of the department. If the department has serious problems, or involves extensive, repetitive systemic issues, or may involve the role of the head of the department, the second-tier investigation will be conducted by an investigation小组 led by the Public Service Commission.

The luxury residence One Stanley has been exposed for steel reinforcement in units not matching the plans. Lee said he would not comment on cases still under investigation, and has asked the Development Bureau to monitor the Buildings Department's investigation.

One Stanley "short on reinforcement" – Development Bureau asked to monitor investigation

Recently, one after another, construction projects have been exposed for problems, including the tilting of lift shafts in the new block of Queen Mary Hospital, concrete samples not meeting standards in a Tung Chung public housing estate, and floor slab steel reinforcement not matching plans at the Stanley luxury residence One Stanley. When asked whether there were problems with construction or even project supervision, Lee responded:

Responding to the One Stanley project issue, Lee said the Buildings Department is seriously investigating the case, "to ascertain whether the construction quality and supervision were adequate, and will deal with it strictly in accordance with the law". Since the investigation is still ongoing, he would not comment on the case details, and has asked the Development Bureau to monitor the investigation. However, he stressed that he attaches great importance to the construction quality of building projects in Hong Kong, "is concerned whether professionals related to the project have performed their supervisory duties diligently, and whether contractors have carried out construction in violation of regulations", and said that this concerns the professional standards, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will inevitably strictly enforce the law.

He has also asked the Development Bureau to improve the legal regulatory requirements and penalties for overall construction projects, to ensure the deterrent effect of legislation, severely punish the relevant personnel in violation, and safeguard the professional standards, quality and safety of Hong Kong's construction projects. The Development Bureau will submit proposed amendments to the Buildings Ordinance this year to strengthen supervision and enhance the disciplinary and penalty systems and penalties, and the authorities will proceed with the relevant work at full speed.

Recent difficulties for nursing graduates in finding jobs have attracted attention. Lee said the demand for nurses has long existed, and pointed out that the Hospital Authority currently has more than 3,000 nurse positions vacant, recruiting medical nurse graduates may apply. (File photo)

Executive Councillor Tommy Cheung criticises "unions impersonating people" – Lee says demand has long existed

Discussion about nurses' difficulty in finding jobs has heated up recently. The trigger was a phone-in programme on a radio station after the Policy Address, where a Mr. Kwok, who claimed to be a psychiatric nurse in the disciplined services, said that his application for deferred retirement had not been approved, and that his nursing graduate daughter was unemployed upon graduation, questioning the Medical Superintendent's introduction of mainland medical staff. Executive Councillor Tommy Cheung later questioned whether it was the union "at any moment impersonating people to make phone calls", and expressed his support for importing foreign talent with raised hands.

Reporters asked about the difficulty for nursing graduates in finding jobs, how to solve the problem of vacancies being concentrated in experienced nurses? How to respond to remarks by Executive Councillors being accused of intensifying social conflicts? Lee said that no matter which industry, there are situations where graduates do not immediately seek employment for various reasons, or where recruiting organisations select the most suitable candidates, "resulting in certain individuals not being hired". He stressed that society's demand for nurses has always existed, especially as Hong Kong's healthcare continues to develop and the population ages, "so the recruitment figures will inevitably reflect these existing demands in the end". He also pointed out, without naming names, that "there are different discussions in society on this aspect, so that everyone can discuss the issue more clearly".

Lee also said that according to the 2025/26 figures, there are about 4,000 potential nursing graduates, and the actual number of applicants to the Hospital Authority is about 2,500, meaning 1,500 are applying for positions outside the Hospital Authority, while the Hospital Authority currently still has more than 3,000 nurse positions vacant, "nursing graduates can apply, and there is a chance of being hired".

Secretary for Health Professor Lo Chung-mau earlier accepted interviews with several media outlets to clarify that the government's recruitment policy must definitely give priority to local talent. Lee also reiterated that according to the current number of nurses in the Hospital Authority, "99.8% are locally trained nurses in Hong Kong", clearly implementing the policy of giving priority to hiring local talent; he also pointed out that currently 40% of nurses work in the public healthcare system, and the remaining 60% work in other medical positions, such as community nursing, elderly care, rehabilitation services, private medical institutions, etc. He stressed that society's demand for nurses exists long-term, and the government will, according to healthcare service needs, exchange views with the industry and the academic sector, and do a good job in planning for healthcare training and manpower development.
